_voted_data_note: Balad has had no MKs since the 25th Knesset (it ran separately in 2022 and did not pass the electoral threshold), so no 25th-Knesset voting data exists for it. As of August 2026 it is polled separately and is in arbitration with Hadash and Ta'al over a possible joint list.

stated_position.source: Balad regards all settlements in the occupied territories as illegal under international law and demands full withdrawal to the 1967 lines
Founding platform: withdrawal to the 1967 borders and an independent Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital, alongside a 'state of all its citizens' inside Israel
Demands an immediate and permanent ceasefire and an end to the war in Gaza
Supports East Jerusalem as the capital of the Palestinian state; opposes exclusive Israeli sovereignty
Supports the Palestinian right of return under UN Resolution 194 as a core, non-negotiable plank
Strongly opposes annexation of any part of the West Bank

Anti-militarist party that rejects military service as the measure of citizenship — its programme demands civic equality independent of service, and it opposes extending conscription frameworks to Arab citizens
Secular democratic party; supports separating religion from the state and civil marriage for all citizens
Secular party; opposes religious coercion in the public sphere
Secular party supporting religious freedom and pluralism, though it takes no active role in intra-Jewish disputes over the Western Wall
Opposes state funding of religious study without obligations, and demands that the same funding logic be applied to Arab education, which is chronically under-funded
Explicitly secular platform — separation of religion and state, opposes state enforcement of religious standards
Social-democratic economic platform; opposes privatisation of strategic infrastructure and supports strong public services
Opposed the 2023 judicial overhaul and the override clause, which it sees as removing the last constraint on majority rule over the Arab minority
Opposes political control of judicial appointments
Supports binding legal oversight of the executive as a check on government power
Supports judicial review of government decisions
Opposed the judicial overhaul and supports judicial independence, while criticising the Israeli courts' own record on the rights of Arab citizens and Palestinians
Flagship demand: Israel as 'a state of all its citizens' with full constitutional equality regardless of ethnicity or religion

Balad has consistently refused to recommend or support Zionist-led governments — it withheld its recommendation from Gantz in 2020 and opposed joining the 2021 change coalition — while backing Arab political participation in principle
Equal per-capita budgeting for Arab municipalities is a central and long-standing demand
Led the opposition to the Nation-State Law, which it regards as constitutionalising the inferior status of Arab citizens
Supports accountability for an indicted prime minister and campaigned against Netanyahu's continued tenure while on trial
Supports term limits as a check on concentrated executive power
The 2014 threshold rise was aimed at the Arab parties and Balad is the party most directly threatened by it; it demands the threshold be lowered
Supports a state commission of inquiry into the failures that led to 7 October and into the conduct of the war
Supports core subjects for all publicly funded schools, coupled with autonomy for Arab education over curriculum, language and national narrative
Supports action against incitement and disinformation in broadcast media targeting Arab citizens, while wary of regulatory powers being used against Arab journalists and outlets
Party bylaws reserve slots for women on the list; supports increased female representation without a formal 50/50 commitment
Supports environmental protection and climate action within an environmental-justice framing (pollution and infrastructure neglect in Arab localities); not a flagship issue
